**Observation Log:**

- [TEMPORAL] Session Date: 2023/05/21 (Sun) 12:35
- [FACT] User has a peace lily and a fiddle leaf fig named Felix.
- [PREFERENCE] User thinks they might have over-fertilized their peace lily.
- [EVENT] User is considering getting a few more plants to add to their collection.
- [CHANGE] User has been using a balanced, water-soluble fertilizer on their African violets, which are doing well.
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] Over-fertilization can cause droopy leaves; user should stop fertilizing for now to allow the peace lily to recover.
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] User should check the soil moisture by sticking their finger into the soil and water only if it feels dry.
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] User should flush the soil by watering the peace lily thoroughly to leach out excess fertilizer salts.
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] User should provide good air circulation for the peace lily and prune any damaged leaves.
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] Peace lilies prefer temperatures between 65°F to 80°F (18°C to 27°C) and moderate humidity.
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] User should consider repotting the peace lily if the soil is heavily contaminated with fertilizer salts.
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] Recommended fertilizers for peace lilies include Miracle-Gro Indoor Plant Food (24-8-16), Schultz All Purpose Plant Food (20-20-20), Espoma Organic Indoor Plant Fertilizer (2-2-2), and E.B. Stone Organics Bloom! (5-3-4).
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] User should follow the instructions on the fertilizer packaging and start with a diluted solution to avoid burning the roots.
- [PREFERENCE] User is considering getting a humidity tray for their peace lily to help with dry air.
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] A humidity tray can increase humidity, reduce transpiration, and prevent leaf tip burn for the peace lily.
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] User should use a shallow tray with pebbles to create a humidity tray and monitor the water level regularly.
- [PREFERENCE] User is thinking of getting low-maintenance plants like succulents or air plants.
- [FACT] User has had good luck with their succulent arrangement on their desk.
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] Succulents are adaptable and require infrequent watering; popular species include Aloe, Echeveria, Crassula, and Sedum.
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] Air plants absorb moisture and nutrients through their leaves; popular species include Tillandsia, Ionantha, and Xerographica.
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] User should provide good light, maintain good air
